verdict: Not pristine yet. The requirement-id mechanism is sound (1202 unique ids, no duplicate, the check green, the allocator idempotent and refusing excluded places), but the marking pass left the text with one rendering defect that is Blocking (60 ids placed before list markers, which turns the numbered step lists of 04 4.2, 08 8.4, 08 8.5 and 12 into single paragraphs, so the steps other pages cite by number no longer exist as steps), fourteen Required defects (a sentence of 10 10.7 split by an inserted paragraph, a stale catalog path in 02 2.1 and 12 12.8, 12 12.11 contradicting its own marking on 06 6.1, 02 2.6 and the [review] rows of 12 12.9, REQ-0024 filed under Ask first, chapter 13 saying v1 where its own vocabulary says L1, an id inserted inside a code span in 03 3.7, a six-cell row in 04 4.3, unescaped pipes in four table cells, 28 ids inside fenced trees, rows and steps the one-per-row rule of 12 12.11 leaves without an id, the invariant cell of I8 without an id while test cells carry ids, an id in a table header of 12 12.2, and 05 5.3's claim that the checks read tables of three pages only) and a handful of Advisory ones. The tool tools/ci reqs is correct for what it checks and well tested; it lacks the placement rules that would have caught the Blocking and three of the Required defects mechanically.
skills_added_beyond_how_to: none: the code under review is a Markdown scanner and allocator with no concurrency, database, CLI framework or dependency change, so golang-modernize, golang-data-structures and golang-troubleshooting would have added no rule the loaded set lacks; the one modernize point (sort.SliceStable, slices.Sorted over maps.Keys, t.Context) is raised from golang-code-style and golang-testing. Skill steps skipped on purpose: no go install, no claude mcp add, no edit to any config file.
lsp: The LSP tool (gopls) was available and used (documentSymbol on tools/ci/reqs.go). Its answer did not match the bytes under review: it listed a type reqRetiredRow at line 251 and reqRetired at line 260, while the file at HEAD 8cc30a8 has no such type and reqRetired at line 256 (every later symbol is off by about nine lines). The spec-req and replan copies of the file are byte-identical and at the same commit, so gopls served a stale or differently resolved buffer. The code findings are judged from the file bytes (Read) and from go vet, go test -race, gofmt -l and golangci-lint 2.14.0 (0 issues), not from the LSP answer.

findings.proposed_change: In tools/ci/reqs.go add to reqIDs (and to the refusal path of reqsAllocate) four findings per mark: (a) 'an id precedes a list marker' when the text before the span is only indentation and the text after it matches `^\s*([0-9]+\.|[-*+])\s`; (b) 'an id sits inside a fenced block' by tracking ``` fences while scanning lines; (c) 'an id sits in a table header row' when the next line is a delimiter row `^\|[\s:|-]+\|$`; (d) 'an id sits inside a code span' when the count of backticks before the span on the line is odd. Add one fixture per rule to TestReqsRules ('an id before a list marker', 'an id inside a fenced block', 'an id in a table header', 'an id inside a code span') and one refusal case per rule to TestReqsAllocate. Cost: about 40 lines of code and four fixtures.

findings.defect: Three smaller points of the tool: (1) reqsAllocate rewrites a page through reqLines (CR LF read as LF) and strings.Join with LF, so a page with CR LF line ends is normalized whole when one placeholder is numbered, a byte change beyond the placeholder that the doc comment does not promise; (2) in reqIDs the retired-row case precedes the placeholder case, so a placeholder typed inside a retired row is silently skipped by the check and never numbered by allocate; (3) the tests cover every rule once but not a CR LF page, a page that is a submodule entry (mode 160000) or a placeholder inside a retired row.
findings.failure_scenario: A page saved by an editor with CR LF ends is rewritten whole by allocate; a `REQ-new` typed into the retired table's Last text cell stays forever and reqs says ok.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Either keep the original line ending per page (split on \n, trim one \r per line, remember whether the file used CR LF, and join with it) or state in the doc comment that allocate writes LF, which hygiene requires anyway; (2) move the placeholder case before the retired-row case so a placeholder is a finding wherever it stands; (3) add the three fixtures to reqs_test.go.

postmortem: After v1.0.0 the first incident this reader sees is a plan task built from a rendered page: an implementer opens 04 4.2 on GitHub, sees the sync procedure as one paragraph, and builds the drift check after the gate because the numbering that fixed their order is gone (finding 1); the pull request cites REQ-0342, the check says covered, and the order is wrong until a journey test fails in block B. The second is a task that cites REQ-0121 and lays out catalog/egress.yaml at the root because 02 2.1 still draws it (finding 3): the catalog surface misses it and gate 1 prints a diff for a file no one meant to ship. Both cross 12 12.11, 04 4.2, 02 2.1 and 10 10.2, and both are caught by the placement rule and the two text fixes above, not by another review round.
lens_critique: L13 (one problem, one mechanism, one name) is the right lens for a pass that added a second naming system to every page, but it reads for contradictions between sentences and is blind to rendering: half of this report is Markdown structure (markers, fences, cells, spans) that only L8 sees, and L8's bullets are about generated docs and guides, not the spec's own pages as rendered artefacts. L6 finds little here because the pass changed no test text. Missing viewpoint among the lens titles: the reader of the rendered page, a Markdown renderer with opinions, who would turn findings 1, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 into one mechanical check (a strict CommonMark lint, which 10 10.2 defers to the pull request that lands tools/ci docs).
out_of_scope: The plan (docs/plan.md, the task files, the inventory JSON): read as context only; whether every live id has a task is the stage-B traceability criterion, measured by tools/ci reqs once the task files cite ids, not by this read.

Whether the 1202 ids are one per obligation everywhere: judged by sampling every page and by the two structural rules (one per row, one per step); a full per-sentence audit of 7 000 lines is a tool's job, and finding 22 is that tool.
The content of lenses.md's new stage-B section and L17 to L21: read for the criteria this review applies, not reviewed.
docs/notes and docs/reference changes of the commit: the two front-matter additions and the ask-first.md regeneration were read and are consistent with the ask-first.yaml change.
confidence: High on the structural findings (each is measured by a script or a grep over the whole set and quoted by line); high on the contradictions (each quotes both sides); medium on the Advisory retire-versus-keep choices of finding 18, which are the operator's call; medium on the tool's exclusion logic for future index sections (it excludes everything after Open questions).
